content.text: All fallback (and nearly all preferred) elements are satisfied, and no other clause caps or unbalances liability.

input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position on its material terms and therefore sits above the fallback. The cap is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability", "The cap is mutual") and is set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. "Fees" (§ 1.5) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other amounts payable under an Order Form, so the 12-month basis is substantive rather than illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually and confirms restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages. Section 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP wholly outside the cap, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not damages. Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and no warranty, indemnity or service-credit clause imposes any lower or one-sided cap. The only point short of the preferred wording is that the payment carve-out is expressed as "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all amounts due; that is a minor sub-element noted here rather than a deviation, so no redline is proposed.
